subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module that builds a low-poly cyberpunk militarized truck using the agentic-3js-builder SDK, sticking to APIs I'm confident about like createBuilder and optional kits (glow, clockwork, pixel, toon), aiming for a correct, runnable 400-600 line script.

I'm structuring the vehicle with a root joint for the hull and separate joints for each wheel (positioned with axle direction along X), since the truck can stay mostly static but the wheels should be riggable to spin. I'm setting dimensions: 7m length, 2.6m width, 3.4m height, with wheels at 0.6m radius sitting on the ground plane, and starting to lay out the chassis as boxes and the cab as an extruded profile, all painted with dark iron materials.

For windows I'll add a simple textured plane, maybe with a sigil emblem on the doors via svg texture. For the cargo container I'm considering using the clockwork kit's panelled and metal materials alongside glow for lights, though I want to be careful about which kit imports are actually available.

Now I'm working out the wheels: lathing a rectangular tyre profile as a shell loop around the hub axis, then figuring out the rim and bolted hub using a ring pattern with frames for positioning.

For the joints, I'm attaching wheel axles with explicit axis directions so the lathe geometry aligns with the local bone orientation. Given the overall complexity, I'll structure the build as a module with helper functions covering wheels, cargo bed, cab, turret and gun, exhaust stacks, antennas, lights, decals, and cyberpunk details like neon strips, cables, and armor plating.

Now I'm laying out the actual coordinate system — the truck faces +Z, width spans roughly -1.3 to 1.3 on x, with the cab toward the front and cargo bed toward the rear, and I'm working out chassis height relative to wheel radius so everything sits at the right ground clearance. I'm also placing the wheels along the x-axis just outside the chassis width, and spacing out front and rear axles along z to give the truck a three-axle stance.

Setting up wheel joints with side-based naming and consistent axle positions, then switching to designing the cab's side profile as an extruded outline using z/y coordinates to shape the windshield, roof, and rear cab wall.

Working through the mirroring logic for the cab shell so both sides stay centered, then opting for a single symmetric extrude rather than separate left/right pieces, with a flat open front for the windshield and a bevel for softer edges.

Now I'm sketching the cab's side profile points for the hood, windshield slope, and roofline, then placing a slanted glass panel as a flat quad defined by four corner points in model space for the windshield.

Positioning the HUD plane slightly offset along its normal so it floats just in front of the glass, then moving on to the hood geometry at the front of the body.

Now I'm sizing the cargo box to sit behind the cab with overlap for a seamless join, giving it a metal panelled texture, and starting to think through cyber armor details like angled side plating on the cargo walls.

I'm planning the lighting and accent elements: an emissive cyan underglow strip along the chassis bottom, magenta neon edges on the cargo corners, a roof turret with a rotating gun barrel built from a rod sweep, twin exhaust stacks behind the cab, a thin antenna with a glowing tip, front ram spikes, and a decal emblem applied to the cargo side panel.

I'm also sketching out hazard stripe paint for the bumper, keeping the body in metal paint while reserving glow effects for flat-colored neon and light parts, adding glowing headlight and taillight spheres, and detailing the wheels with lathed tires, rims, hub cylinders, and a bolt ring pattern.

Now I'm wiring up the joint hierarchy: wheels parented to the hull with outward-facing frames depending on left/right side, a turret joint on the hull, and a gun joint on the turret using an aim target point for orientation, plus a barrel rod connecting them.

Switching to the tire geometry, I'm defining the lathe outline for the tread with rounded shoulder points, then separate lathe shapes for the rim as an annulus and a small hub cylinder, all oriented along the X axis and attached to the wheel bone.

Setting up the wheel-building loop across axle positions and left/right sides, assigning colors (dark tire rubber, steel rim, glowing cyan hub accent), then moving on to the front bumper box with hazard stripes and ram spikes.

Adding headlight spheres with warm glow, red tail lights on the cargo rear, and neon edge strips along the cargo corners glowing magenta.

Still placing lighting and detail elements... cyan underglow strip beneath the chassis, cable sweeps connecting cab to cargo using a catmull curve, and dual exhaust stacks positioned just behind the cab.

I'm positioning the exhaust stacks between the cab and cargo, then adding an antenna as a thin swept curve rising from the cargo roof near the turret, capped with a small glowing tip sphere.

Now I'm building the roof turret: a lathe-shaped base, a boxy housing mounted on a turret joint, and a gun joint aiming forward so the barrel can be attached as a rod with a glowing muzzle tip, all parented so the gun rotates with the turret.

I'm sketching out the cargo module's decal placement for a side emblem, mapping the texture onto the cargo part at a specific position and size, and considering adding seam panels to the rear cargo doors for visual detail.

Now I'm working through the side armor skirts, calculating their extrude outline and placement relative to the chassis and wheel widths to make sure the plates sit correctly above the wheels without clipping.

I'm choosing materials for each major section: panelled iron for the body and cargo with slight polish or tarnish variation, a bluish tone for the cab, and a dark slab color for the glass. I'll import panelled and metal helpers along with a glow effect, then plan out remaining details like bumper stripes, overall part count, and wheel bolt rings.

Writing ring and glow code...

Now I'm sketching the cab outline profile, checking roof height against the cargo box height to make sure they overlap sensibly for a militarized-truck look, then planning to extrude that outline along the x-axis.

Mapping out the hood and front bumper box dimensions and positions relative to the cab, and figuring out metal paint for the cab panels before placing spikes on the bumper base.

I'm sizing the chassis, cargo box, and cab so they stack correctly: chassis spans most of the length, the cargo box sits on top of the chassis, and the headlights are flush-mounted on the front bumper. Now I'm working out the windshield's slanted slab points to connect the hood to the cab roofline.

Computing the HUD plane's normal vector and position relative to the windshield slope...

For the HUD texture itself, I'm designing an SVG with a dark cyan-tinted background, horizontal status bars, a bracketed readout box, and "SIGNAL 97" text to give it a sci-fi targeting display feel.

Writing SVG code...

For the cargo details, I'm adding glowing magenta corner strips, a tail light, and a dark metal rear seam, then placing emblem decals on both flanks of the cargo using opposing direction vectors so they mirror correctly on left and right sides.

For the bumper, I'm painting hazard stripes in dark ink and yellow, then arranging a row of steel spikes along the front edge with slight upward-forward tilts. Now I'm starting the side armor plate geometry, defining extrusion points along the vehicle's flank.

Mirroring the skirt plates on both sides with small thickness and bevel in a polished iron finish, then setting up the wheel axle positions (front, mid, rear) and looping through left/right sides to build joints, tires, and rims at each wheel center.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Still placing the bolt ring...

For the cab, I'm working out door seam details, side window slabs, and figuring out the window polygon positions on the cab side panels.

I'm also sketching in a rooftop light bar for the cab, sizing a thin box near the roofline and deciding on its color.

For remaining details, I'm adding a cable sweeping from the cab to the cargo side using a thin catmull curve, plus a rear bumper box positioned just behind the chassis end, and small amber glowing sidelights.

Now I'm positioning exhaust stacks as cylinders rising from the body near the cab-cargo junction, with glowing orange tip caps. I'm also setting up the root joint for the rigged model and explicitly binding body parts to it, then starting to define the turret joint.

For the turret, I'm lathing out a pedestal profile and adding a housing box, then defining a gun joint with a barrel built from stacked rod segments of increasing thickness toward the muzzle, finishing with a glowing sphere at the muzzle tip for a brake effect.

I'm adding an ammo box on the cargo deck, then working out the cab's front grille and headlight placement relative to the hood geometry, positioning small spheres for the headlights on either side of the grille.

Now I'm setting up stripe and panel paint patterns for the bumper and cargo body using the SDK's paint helpers, checking that the stripes/panelled functions resolve colors correctly, and confirming the part/slab/extrude call signatures I'll need for the remaining details.

I'm defining color constants for steel, glass, tires, bolts, and neon accent hues, then setting up glow effects and ring patterns before starting on the antenna geometry.

Now I'm working through cable paths connecting cab and cargo, checking for geometry collisions with the skirt and adjusting the route to avoid overlap.

I'm placing exhaust stacks, roof spotlights, and considering side vent slats on the cargo, but deciding to skip the slats since they'd overlap with the skirt and emblem decal.

Given the user wants an extremely intricate build with 180-340 parts across 700+ lines, I'm planning to expand further with cargo ribs, roof armor plates, grill slats, wheel arch covers, spikes, underglow, a rear ladder, and side mirrors to flesh out the module to around 300 lines.

Writing the module imports and color palette...

Building the chassis with underglow lighting, then adding the cargo box with emblem decals mirrored on both sides...

Adding rib detailing...

Now I'm planning the rear elements like door seams, tail lights, neon strips, bumper, and plate, then the front details including hood, grille, bumper, spikes, headlights, windshield, and cab structure with its extruded shape.

Shaping cab geometry, mirrors, exhaust stacks, and roof bar...

Still planning components: windshield, wheel arch skirts, turret, gun, ammo box, antenna, wheels, front spikes, bumper hazard lights, emblem text, and verifying return structure for the root builder.

I'm checking frame and ring signatures, confirming the HUD glow plane placement with dir and axis, and verifying glass slab placement is fine without extra glow. For the wheels, I'm working out the tyre lathe profile, rim annulus, hub cylinder, and glow disc dimensions to make sure everything nests correctly in radius and axial spans.

Now I'm adding bolt rings around the hub using a radial frame pattern with small cylinders, and finalizing the lathe wheel geometry bound to the bone. Then I'll write out the complete module with brief comments, aiming for roughly 250 lines.
